### approvedGrantSchema

```ts
const approvedGrantSchema: ZodReadonly<
  ZodObject<
    {
      capability: ZodPipe<
        ZodUnknown,
        ZodTransform<
          | "agent.list"
          | "agent.manage"
          | "agent.rename"
          | "agent.toolPolicy"
          | "agent.read"
          | "agent.send"
          | "computer.list"
          | "computer.readFile"
          | "computer.writeFile"
          | "computer.execute"
          | "llm.generation"
          | "media.generation"
          | "games:servers"
          | "git.repository"
          | "apps.open"
          | "apps.call"
          | "app.storage"
          | "app.events.emit"
          | "team.workbenchHost"
          | "marketplace.browse"
          | "marketplace.purchase"
          | "workflow.run"
          | "workflow.publish"
          | "workflow.arm"
          | "world"
          | "channels.read"
          | "channels.personal.manage",
          unknown
        >
      >;
      capabilityApproved: ZodLiteral<true>;
      operations: ZodReadonly<ZodArray<ZodString>>;
      resources: ZodUnion<
        readonly [
          ZodLiteral<"tenant-scope">,
          ZodReadonly<
            ZodArray<
              ZodReadonly<
                ZodObject<
                  {
                    kind: ZodString;
                    id: ZodString;
                  },
                  $strict
                >
              >
            >
          >,
        ]
      >;
    },
    $strict
  >
>;
```

Consent approves capabilities, with explicit operation and resource ceilings. A
Release adding a method that requires an already-approved capability needs no
new consent; a new capability does. Release selection intersects stored
operations instead of adding approvals. Each Worker call is still restricted to
that method's declared requires, never the App's complete capability set. Only
an approved install or set-grants command mints capabilityApproved. Empty
operation rows retain that consent; removing the capability revokes it.
route:app.methods rows record approval detail, not a method allowlist: narrowing
them in set-grants does not restrict methods using an approved capability. Exact
operation rows are enforced for capability routes and backend bindings.

### appToolPolicySchema

```ts
const appToolPolicySchema: Struct<{
  level: Literals<readonly ["read", "write"]>;
  revision: NonEmptyString;
  grantedBy: NonEmptyString;
}>;
```

One App-tool access level, with its own freshness pin. An Agent's comes from the
owner's stored direct approval; a key's is computed fresh from its own Ear Tag
grants (`keyAppAccess`), never stored as this shape -- only read through it, for
one call or one installation at a time.

### admitMethodMetadata()

```ts
function admitMethodMetadata(facts, name): AppMethodMetadataDecision;
```

Check a verified method's Release, principal, effect and real capability
consent. Captures have no mapped runtime input yet. This result cannot authorize
execution: dispatch must still use admits, including its ordinary input
validation. Input schemas are not compiled here; execution may still refuse
invalid_input. Project captured bindings with appInvocationCeiling(facts).

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                      |
| --------- | ------------------------- |
| `facts`   | [`GateFacts`](#gatefacts) |
| `name`    | `string`                  |

#### Returns

[`AppMethodMetadataDecision`](#appmethodmetadatadecision)
